title: Northbridge Analytics - embed pilot scoping & hosting options
summary: Discovery call to scope an embeddings + rerank pilot. Northbridge is evaluating tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) for a retail search product. Key constraints: sub-120ms 95th percentile on query path, burst throughput for Black Friday, SOC2 + SSO requirement, and desire to keep raw user text out of third-party storage. Next steps: send security deck, pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated pilot, and propose benchmark plan (10k QPS simulation and 1M vector dataset).
topics: rerank architecture and vector DB integration
next_steps: Jordan: share security & SOC2 + architecture deck by 2027-11-08
Priya: propose pilot benchmark plan and test script by 2027-11-10
Alex: provide sample query distribution and 1k sample documents by 2027-11-09
Schedule technical smoke test on Redwood Dedicated with 1k qps window week of 2027-11-15

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-05 16:00 UTC — Duration 48 minutes — Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Northbridge Head of Search), Maya Chen (SRE), Sam Park (Data Eng), Nora Li (PM)

Summary: quick intros, current pain points, discuss hosting choices, go deep on rerank flow and vector DB hit patterns, agree next steps for pilot.

00:00:05 Jordan (AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. want to kick off with quick intros?
00:00:15 Alex: sure I'm Alex head of search at Northbridge, we run search for our retail clients, low latency, high throughput, need better relevance.
00:00:22 Maya: Maya, infra, i'll be looking at networking and security
00:00:25 Sam: Sam, data eng, we'll own the pipeline and embeddings
00:00:28 Nora: Nora product, prioritizing relevance metrics and experiment cadence
00:00:32 Priya (SE): Great, thanks. quick framing: we find most customers evaluating embeddings + rerank consider 1) where to serve embeddings (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 2) embedding dims and model choice, and 3) rerank latency cost tradeoffs. curious — what are your top constraints today?
00:00:48 Alex: latency first, we want tail lat under 120 ms for interactive search recency, and at peak traffic (holiday spikes) we need bursts of about 5k qps across the system, not all vector lookups but aggregate. also data residency: we cannot ship raw user text to third-party stores by policy — so that pushes toward VPC or private.
00:01:05 Jordan: got it, makes sense. are you currently using a vector DB?
00:01:09 Sam: yes we use Pine-cone (Pinecone) for nearest neighbors, but we keep rerank models in-house; the bottleneck now is throughput — the pinecone cost and latency when fanout is large.
00:01:20 Priya (SE): thanks, and what embedding dim do you use today?
00:01:24 Sam: 1536 right now from an in-house transformer. debating if we move to 768 or quantized 1536 to save storage/cost.
00:01:31 Alex: also experiment velocity — we want quick A/B tests on embedding models without full infra changes.
00:01:35 Priya (SE): okay, lots to unpack. a couple of things from the Redwood side: Hosted API gives fastest time-to-value but raw text and embeddings are processed in Redwood's hosted infra; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools (predictable latency and throughput) without multi-tenant interference; Private we offer as VPC or on-prem which keeps data in your network and integrates with your KMS.
00:01:56 Maya: what about SSO and audit logs? SOC2?
00:02:00 Jordan: we support SAML/SSO and RBAC, and we can provide SOC2 Type II reports — we'll attach the security deck. audit logs for inference and key actions are available in Redwood Console.
00:02:10 Maya: good. you mentioned KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
00:02:13 Priya (SE): yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Hosted can also support BYOK in certain configurations — we can detail that in the deck.
00:02:21 Sam: on the rerank flow — our architecture is: user query -> embedding -> vector DB fanout top-200 -> re-ranker on top-20, run cross-attention model. most cost is cross-attention re-ranker. we want to reduce tokens/cost there.
00:02:36 Priya (SE): that's a common pattern. options to reduce cost: reduce fanout with better recall at top-k via hybrid search, do a cheap semantic skimming embedding or use condensed embeddings, or quantize embeddings and use smaller rerank models with feature distillation. have you tried hybrid search (bm25 + vector) or rerank-first?
00:02:56 Alex: BM25 helps for exact matches but hurts on semantic queries. we were hoping to use dynamic fanout based on confidence score. if we could do a quick score-based fallback that'd be ideal.
00:03:05 Jordan (AE): Redwood has routing policies and caching — you can do per-request policies to route to Hosted models or cheaper variants. also automatic KV/prefix caching can shave a lot of repeated-query cost.
00:03:16 Priya (SE): for throughput numbers, can you share expected qps and dataset size?
00:03:20 Alex: current prod is about 800 qps average, spikes to 4k qps. corpus is around 8 million documents, vector index size ~ 1M active documents after filtering for product catalog.
00:03:33 Sam: we also have lots of short queries — tail latency matters more than average.
00:03:37 Priya (SE): okay for a pilot we usually suggest: 1) a Dedicated reserved capacity smoke test for 1k qps sustained with burst to 3k qps, 2) run an offline benchmark with your sample corpus (1M vectors) to measure recall/latency at k=100 and downstream rerank cost. we can also run the index on our hosting with your VPC peering for private connectivity.
00:03:58 Nora: timeline question — how fast can you stand up a dedicated pilot?
00:04:02 Jordan: typically 1-2 weeks for a Dedicated sandbox; Private VPC takes longer (2-4 weeks) depending on approvals. Hosted is immediate.
00:04:09 Alex: for compliance we probably need VPC, but want to see economics on Dedicated first. cost sensitivity: cross-attention rerank is the big driver. any suggestions to reduce token cost?
00:04:20 Priya (SE): a few levers: 1) quantize rerank models (int8 or int4) for lower GPU memory and throughput gains, 2) use a cascade approach — small classifier to narrow candidates then run expensive reranker, 3) reduce embed dims or use asymmetric embeddings (compact index, larger reranker). for embeddings storage cost we can reduce from 1536->768 with small recall tradeoff; we'll show numbers in the pilot plan.
00:04:44 Sam: curious about latency numbers on Dedicated — do you provide tail metrics and guaranteed SLOs?
00:04:48 Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets and predictable throughput; Console has token-level latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards to trace tail. we'll share typical 95th percentile numbers from similar customers.
00:04:59 Maya: networking — if we do VPC peering, how does tokenization/sensitive payloads flow? do you store any raw queries?
00:05:06 Priya (SE): with Private VPC we can ensure no raw text leaves your VPC; logs can be shipped to your logging endpoints. for Hosted we retain minimal logs for metrics but can enable stricter retention and encryption. details in the security doc.
00:05:16 Alex: great. on vector DB integration — we currently push vectors to Pinecone. can Redwood call out-of-process vector DBs or do you want customers to host indices on Redwood infra?
00:05:25 Priya (SE): both patterns supported. you can keep your vector DB (Pinecone, Weeviate, Milvus) and call Redwood for embeddings and rerank, or you can host the index in Redwood Dedicated for faster fanout and lower network hops. many customers keep control of index for compliance but colocate compute in Dedicated for latency.
00:05:44 Sam: would colocating index inside Dedicated remove the Pinecone cost entirely?
00:05:48 Jordan: yes depending on the pilot; you'd replace the third-party vector DB cost with Redwood Dedicated capacity cost — often cheaper at scale because of optimized kernels and batching.
00:05:57 Priya (SE): and Redwood has hybrid-search features — you can do approximate ANN inside Dedicated optimized on GPU and fall back to the DB if needed.
00:06:08 Alex: ok let's talk numbers — sample pricing and what a pilot looks like?
00:06:12 Jordan: i'll send an initial pricing comparison: Hosted per-token + embedding units; Dedicated monthly reserved capacity with a pilot discount; Private includes setup + licensing. for the pilot we can do a 4-week smoke test with a defined load profile.
00:06:24 Nora: we need a pass/fail criteria — what should we measure?
00:06:27 Priya (SE): suggested success criteria: 1) 95th percentile query path < 120ms under pilot load; 2) recall@20 within 3% of current baseline or improved; 3) rerank cost per query reduced by at least 20% vs current run-rate or same cost with improved relevance.
00:06:43 Alex: sounds reasonable. for benchmarks — we can anonymize logs and share sample corpora, what's the recommended format?
00:06:48 Priya (SE): CSV with query, timestamp, and doc IDs, plus the doc corpus as JSONL. we'll include a spec in the follow-up.
00:06:55 Sam: curious about embedding storage and dimensionality — what are tradeoffs for 1536 vs 768 in production?
00:07:01 Priya (SE): 1536 gives better recall usually, but doubles storage and indexing cost versus 768; throughput also depends on index algorithm. we can run both in pilot to measure delta. quantization can reduce storage significantly with small recall hit.
00:07:13 Alex: any rough guidance on reranker model sizes and token costs?
00:07:16 Jordan: for cross-attention rerank models, many customers move to smaller distilled models (like 110M-350M) for rerank or use a 1-stage bi-encoder + lightweight cross-attention only on top candidates. that reduces token/GPU compute cost drastically.
00:07:29 Maya: monitoring — can we get token-level cost breakouts so product can see cost per query by path?
00:07:33 Priya (SE): yes Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model; you can also instrument trace hooks.
00:07:40 Alex: ok next steps and timeline?
00:07:43 Jordan: recap: we'll send security deck + SOC2, pricing and pilot contract, and a benchmark plan. you will share anonymized logs and sample corpus. propose to start Dedicated sandbox week of 2027-11-15.
00:07:55 Nora: thanks — when can we expect the docs?
00:07:58 Jordan: security deck and pricing by Monday 2027-11-08, Priya's benchmark script by 2027-11-10.
00:08:05 Alex: great. anything else?
00:08:07 Maya: one more Q, does Redwood support per-tenant encryption and separate index per tenant?
00:08:12 Priya (SE): yes multitenant isolation patterns supported — Dedicated can isolate pools and Private gives fully separate control plane. we'll include patterns in the follow-up.
00:08:20 Sam: ok thanks everyone we'll get the logs over.
00:08:23 Jordan: awesome, thanks for your time — we'll follow up with the package.
00:08:28 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription had a few proper noun mismatches (Pinecone transcribed as Pine-cone, Weaviate as Weeviate) and a generic speaker label slipped in (Speaker 3).

References shared during call: security deck link (internal): https://redwood.company/sales/security-deck-northbridge (placeholder), pilot-plan doc: https://redwood.company/pilot/northbridge-harness (placeholder).
